0.long_answer: Necrotizing enterocolitis is a severe intestinal disease that predominantly affects premature or very low birth weight infants. This condition involves inflammation and bacterial invasion of the intestinal wall, which can quickly progress to necrosis of the affected bowel segments. In cases where the necrosis is extensive, surgical removal of the damaged portions of the small intestine may be necessary. This reduction in the functional length of the intestine can result in short bowel syndrome, a condition characterized by malabsorption and nutritional deficiencies.
